title: Open WebUI -- T1059.007 caller-supplied session_id delivers code-interpreter events to another user
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59216 (CVSS 7.7 HIGH), affecting
Open WebUI prior to 0.10.0.

`get_event_call()` delivers `execute:python` and `execute:tool`
Socket.IO events to whatever `session_id` a caller supplies, checking
only that the session is currently CONNECTED --
`if session_id not in SESSION_POOL: return {'error': ...}` -- never
whether the session belongs to the requesting caller. A victim's live
`session_id` is separately disclosed to any read-access participant of
a shared document via the `ydoc:document:join` event. Chained: an
attacker (1) shares a document with the victim to learn the victim's
`session_id` via `ydoc:document:join`, then (2) sends
`POST /api/v1/chat/completions` with the victim's `session_id` embedded
in the request body, causing the server to deliver an
`execute:python`/`execute:tool` event to the VICTIM's browser session --
running the attacker's code interpreter payload as the victim (full RCE
if the victim holds admin privileges).

Detection logic flags the discriminating half of this chain that a log
source can actually observe: a chat-completions request whose body
carries a `session_id` value that does NOT match the session the
HTTP/WebSocket connection itself authenticated as -- the fix's own
remediation is exactly this ownership check
(`session.get('id') != request_info.get('user_id')`), so a mismatch on
an unpatched deployment is the vulnerability's precise trigger.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, which quotes both the vulnerable code and the fix's
ownership-check logic), fixed in 0.10.0.
